common_name: Nonstop Flame Begonia (Compact Upright Fiery Orange-Red Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, then move outdoors to containers or shaded beds once frost danger has passed.

directions: Grow in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil or containers in partial to full shade, away from hot midday sun. Nonstop Flame produces fully double, rose-form blooms in a hot blend of orange and red tones over the series' signature tight, mounded habit, giving a brighter, more flickering color effect than the solid true-red Nonstop Red. Feed lightly every few weeks through the growing season to sustain continuous flowering from late spring to frost. Lift and store tubers dry over winter wherever the ground freezes, replanting after the danger of frost has passed.
sources: Benary - Begonia tuberhybrida F1 Nonstop series product page

common_name: Nonstop Peach Shades Begonia (Compact Upright Soft Peach Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into shaded beds or containers once frost danger has passed.

directions: Plant in rich, evenly moist, well-draining soil or containers in partial to full shade. Nonstop Peach Shades carries softly blended peach and apricot tones across its fully double flowers, giving a gentler pastel presence than the series' saturated reds and oranges such as Nonstop Flame. The compact, self-branching mound needs no pinching and flowers continuously from late spring through the first hard frost with routine watering and light monthly feeding. Dig and store tubers dry over winter in cold-winter regions, replanting once soil has warmed the following spring.
sources: Benary - Begonia tuberhybrida F1 Nonstop series product page

common_name: Nonstop Lemon Begonia (Compact Upright Pale Yellow Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, then set out in containers or shaded beds once nighttime temperatures stay reliably above 50F.

directions: Site in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil or containers in partial to full shade. Nonstop Lemon bears fully double blooms in a light, clear pale yellow, a cooler and softer tone than the deeper gold of the series' Yellow selection, set against the series' tidy, compact mound of glossy foliage. Keep soil consistently moist but never waterlogged, and feed lightly every few weeks to support continuous flowering into fall. Where winters bring hard freezes, lift tubers after foliage dieback and store them dry until spring replanting.
sources: Benary - Begonia tuberhybrida F1 Nonstop series product page

common_name: Nonstop Orange Begonia (Compact Upright Bright Orange Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into containers or shaded beds once frost danger has passed.

directions: Grow in rich, well-drained soil or containers in partial to full shade, protected from hot afternoon sun. Nonstop Orange produces fully double, rose-form flowers in a clean, saturated orange that is more uniform than the orange-red blend of Nonstop Flame, held above a dense, compact mound of glossy foliage. It flowers continuously from late spring until the first hard frost without deadheading, tolerating humid summer weather well. Lift and store tubers dry over winter in any climate where the ground freezes, replanting the following spring after frost danger has passed.
sources: Benary - Begonia tuberhybrida F1 Nonstop series product page

common_name: Nonstop Salmon Begonia (Compact Upright Coral-Salmon Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks ahead of the last frost, then move outdoors to containers or beds in partial to full shade once frost danger has passed.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil or containers in partial to full shade. Nonstop Salmon carries fully double blooms in a warm coral-salmon shade that sits between pink and orange tones, displayed over the series' dense, mounded habit. The compact plants need no pinching and bloom steadily from late spring through frost with regular watering and light monthly feeding. In climates where tubers cannot overwinter outdoors, dig and store them in a cool, dry, frost-free spot once foliage dies back.
sources: Benary - Begonia tuberhybrida F1 Nonstop series product page

common_name: Nonstop Pink Begonia (Compact Upright Clear Pink Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into shaded containers or beds once frost danger has passed.

directions: Site in rich, evenly moist, well-draining soil or containers in partial to full shade. Nonstop Pink bears fully double, camellia-form flowers in a clear, true pink that reads lighter and cooler than the deeper magenta-rose of Nonstop Deep Rose, over the series' compact, self-branching mound. Flowering continues steadily from late spring to the first hard frost without deadheading, holding up well through humid summer weather. Where winters bring hard freezes, lift and store tubers dry indoors, replanting once the soil has warmed the following spring.

common_name: Nonstop Deep Rose Begonia (Compact Upright Dark Magenta-Pink Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, then set out in partial to full shade once frost danger has passed.

directions: Grow in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil or containers in partial to full shade. Nonstop Deep Rose produces fully double flowers in a rich, dark magenta-pink that is noticeably more intense than the lighter Nonstop Pink, carried on the series' tight, dome-shaped mound of glossy foliage. The self-branching habit requires no pinching and keeps flowering from late spring through the first frost with consistent moisture and light monthly feeding. Lift and store tubers dry over winter wherever the ground freezes, replanting the following spring.

common_name: Nonstop Rose Picotee Begonia (Compact Upright Rose-Edged White Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into containers or shaded beds once frost danger has passed.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained soil or containers in partial to full shade. Nonstop Rose Picotee is distinguished within the Nonstop line by a fine rose-pink edge rimming each otherwise pale petal, a bicolor picotee pattern not found on the series' solid-color selections like Nonstop White or Nonstop Pink. The compact, mounded habit blooms continuously from late spring through the first hard frost with regular watering and light monthly feeding. Dig and store tubers dry over winter in cold climates, replanting after the danger of frost has passed in spring.

common_name: Illumination Lemon Begonia (Trailing Pale Yellow Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and move hanging baskets or containers outdoors to shade once frost danger has passed.

directions: Grow in a rich, well-drained potting mix in hanging baskets or raised containers in partial to full shade, where the trailing stems can cascade freely. Illumination Lemon carries pale, clear yellow double flowers on the same vigorously trailing, heat-tolerant habit shared by other Illumination colors such as Illumination Orange and Illumination White, giving a soft citrus tone for mixed basket plantings. Keep the growing medium evenly moist and feed every few weeks through the season to sustain bloom production into fall. Overwinter tubers indoors in cold climates, storing them dry and frost-free until replanting the following spring.
sources: Benary - Begonia tuberhybrida F1 Illumination series product page

common_name: Illumination Scarlet Begonia (Trailing True-Red Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into hanging baskets or shaded containers once frost danger has passed.

directions: Plant in a rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained mix in hanging baskets or containers kept in partial to full shade. Illumination Scarlet brings a saturated true-red double flower to the trailing Illumination series, reading darker and more intense than the softer Illumination Rose, cascading over the same vigorous, heat-tolerant stems. Water regularly and feed lightly every few weeks to maintain continuous flowering from early summer through fall. In regions with freezing winters, dig and store tubers dry indoors over the dormant season for replanting the next year.
sources: Benary - Begonia tuberhybrida F1 Illumination series product page

common_name: Illumination Salmon Pink Begonia (Trailing Coral-Pink Tuberous Begonia)

Illumination Salmon Pink produces double flowers in a warm coral-pink blend, a softer and more orange-tinged shade than the cooler Illumination Rose, over the series' vigorously trailing, heat-tolerant stems.
